newsitem.title: USA: Rouge Steel boosts blast furnace output, earnings.
newsitem.headline: Rouge Steel boosts blast furnace output, earnings.

text.p: Rouge Steel Co. said Tuesday its first quarter earnings rose by 39 percent, boosted by improved production from its own blast furnaces and a bigger share of the automotive sheet steel market.

Rouge Steel, which operates a single integrated mill in Dearborn, reported first quarter net income of $9.3 million, or 42 cents a share, up from $6.7 million, or 31 cents a share, during the first quarter of 1996.
Steel product shipments in the first quarter totalled 744,000 tons, up 42,000 tons, or 6 percent from the year-ago period, reflecting record shipments to the automotive sector.

The company said its raw steel production totalled 748,000 tons in the January-March period, an increase of 94,000 tons over the first quarter of 1996 and 228,000 tons over the fourth quarter of 1996, when production was hurt by relining work on its biggest blast furnace.

"We are pleased with the steady increase in blast furnace production since the reline of our largest blast furnace in the fourth quarter of 1996," Rouge Steel Chairman Carl Valdiserri said in a statement.

Valdiserri said the company planned to upgrade its primary steel production facilities in the fourth quarter of 1997 and will improve its hot strip mill and tandem mill as part of an effort to reduce costs, boost improve quality and enhance product offerings.
"Our order book continues to be strong through the second quarter and we expect 1997 to be a good year," Valdiserri said.
